privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.intro: This policy explains what personal information MTB3A collects, why we use it, who receives it, how long we keep it and what rights you have. It covers MTB3A's website, its web portal, whether you sign in or try it on your own device, and its iPhone and Android apps. It is part of our terms of service, and it does not cover any other product.

scope.title: The short version
scope.body: MTB3A keeps the records of who owes you money, what came in and what went out. When you sign in, what you enter (clients, projects, income, expenses, receipts and, if you issue them, tax documents) is saved to our servers so it's there on every device you sign in on. If you try the portal without an account, your records stay in that browser and never reach us. We use your information to run MTB3A for you, to meet our legal duties and to keep the service secure. Our website sends us what you type in the account-request form, only if you fill it in and press Send, and it counts visits anonymously, as described under "Anonymous usage counts". Each visit to its home page also asks our servers whether sign-up and the free plan are open, as described under "What reaches the network". None of our apps use ads or tracking, and we never sell your data.

whoWeAre.title: Who is responsible for your information
whoWeAre.body: MTB3A is owned and provided by Barmajiyat Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales under company number 17082456, registered office 65 London Wall, London, United Kingdom, ("we", "us"). Narabnd Studio Ltd (נאראבנד סטודיו בע"מ), company number 517108775, Az-Zahra St. 18, Jerusalem, a related company, is MTB3A's registered software house with the Israel Tax Authority: it holds the connection to the Tax Authority and signs the documents you issue, under a licence from us. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q3, Q4): Narabnd's role for issued documents (holder or processor), who owns the account database in Israel, and whether a data processing agreement is needed.] For your account details (your name, email address, sign-in, settings and billing), we decide how they are used: under Israel's Protection of Privacy Law we are the owner of that database, and under the GDPR its controller. The records you keep about your own clients, suppliers and work are yours to decide on. For those we act on your behalf, only to run MTB3A for you: you are their owner, and we hold them for you (a holder under the Protection of Privacy Law, a processor under the GDPR), as our terms of service describe. You are responsible for having the right to record your clients' details and for telling them about it where the law requires. The Protection of Privacy Law requires a privacy protection officer, and the registration of a database, only for databases above certain sizes or of certain kinds; ours are below them today, so we have not appointed an officer or registered a database. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q4): confirm the thresholds.] If that changes, we will do what the law requires and name the officer here.

lawAndPurposes.title: Why we use your information, and the law we follow
lawAndPurposes.body: We handle personal information under Israel's Protection of Privacy Law, 5741-1981, as amended (including Amendment 13, in force since August 2025), and the Protection of Privacy (Data Security) Regulations, 5777-2017, and, where they apply to you, the EU and UK GDPR. We use your information only for these purposes: to create and run your account and give you the features you use (to perform our agreement with you); to issue the documents you ask for, keep the records the law requires and answer lawful requests from authorities (to meet legal obligations); to keep MTB3A secure, prevent fraud and abuse, fix faults and improve the service (our legitimate interest in running a safe, working service); and to count usage in the portal and the apps, only if you agree, which you can withdraw at any time (your consent). No law requires you to give us information, but without an email address we can't open an account, and without your business details we can't issue tax documents for you. We don't make decisions about you by automated means alone, and we never sell your information or use it for advertising.

mobile.title: iPhone and Android: your account and our servers
mobile.body: The mobile apps need an account. While sign-up is open you can create one yourself on the hosted portal, as described under "When you create an account"; otherwise your organization or we set one up for you. When you sign in, we keep your email address, display name, language, and which business profiles you can use. What you enter is stored on MTB3A's servers, and a copy is kept on your phone so the app works offline. Entries you make while offline are saved on your phone and uploaded once you're back online. Signing out ends your session on our servers. Entries that haven't uploaded yet stay on the phone and upload after you sign in again.

hostedAccounts.title: Where your records live
hostedAccounts.body: Your account (the web portal, and the iPhone and Android apps when you're signed in) keeps your records on MTB3A's servers in Google Cloud's europe-west1 region (Belgium), and our daily backups stay there too. We keep each backup for 14 days, and we can restore your records to any moment in the last 7 days. Google Cloud encrypts your records, receipts and backups where they are stored, and our servers reach the database only over encrypted connections. Our servers' technical logs are kept by Google Cloud for 30 days, and may be stored outside the europe-west1 region. With your account we also keep, for each place you're signed in, a shortened description of your browser or app (never your IP address); for each passkey you add, its public key and identifier, never your fingerprint or face; and for each email we send you, a scrambled form of your address and whether it arrived, for 30 days. MTB3A is run by a small team, and the people who run it can technically reach your data. We look at your records only when you ask us to help, to fix a fault, or when the law requires it, and changes made with our admin tools are logged. Error reports go to Sentry in the EU, as described under "Error reports". Usage counts from the portal and the apps go to PostHog in the EU only if you agree; our website counts visits anonymously, as described under "Anonymous usage counts". What happens when you close your account is described under "Deleting your account and data". Accounts are also covered by our terms of service.

createAccount.title: When you create an account
createAccount.body: While sign-up is open, you can create an account yourself on the hosted portal. You type your email address and we email you a link that works for 24 hours; your account is created only when you open that link and set a password. Until then we keep only your address and the page's language with the link, and we delete them about a week after the link expires. The sign-up and password-recovery forms first run a check with Cloudflare Turnstile to tell people from bots. Turnstile receives your IP address and details about your browser and device, and never what you type into the form. To check that your address can receive email, our servers look up its domain (the part after the @) in public DNS records, and ask the domain's registry, through its public registration records (RDAP), when the domain was registered. Only the domain name is sent in these lookups, never the rest of your address. We don't accept addresses from disposable email services or at domains that can't receive email. Sign-ups from personal email providers or email-forwarding services, and from domains these lookups can't confirm (for example, one registered in the last 90 days), are reviewed by our team before the account opens; we keep the domain and the reason for the review with it, and we email you the outcome.

email.title: Emails we send
email.body: We email you only about your account: the link to finish creating it or to set a new password, a reminder that you already have an account if you try to sign up again, a notice when your password changes or a passkey is added to your account, a notice that we're reviewing your sign-up and then its outcome, a sign-in code when you ask for one, two-step sign-in codes and a notice when two-step sign-in is turned on, off or changed, notices that your free trial is ending or has moved you to the free Starter plan, that your account has become read-only, that a card payment failed, that a discounted first year is about to renew at the regular price, and that your profile's connection to the Israel Tax Authority needs renewing, and, when you close your account, a notice with the day it will be deleted. If your paid plan ends, we may also email you up to twice, about 30 and 90 days later, with an offer to come back. That offer is the only promotional email we send. It always has an Unsubscribe link, and it works with your email app's own unsubscribe button; turning offers off never stops the emails your account needs. Every promotional email is labelled «פרסומת» (Hebrew for "advertisement") at the start of its subject, whatever language it is written in, and carries our details as its sender: Barmajiyat Ltd, our address and how to contact us. If you invite an accountant, we also email them an invite, as described under "Sharing with your accountant". It goes to the address you give us, and we use that address only for the invite and to show you who you invited. Once a month, while you pay, try or use the free Starter plan, we email you a summary of the month before: per profile and per currency, what came in, what's still owed and what's overdue. You can turn it off with the link in it or in You › Account. Our other emails never include amounts or your records, and we don't track whether you open any of them or click their links. We send them through Resend, which receives your email address, the message and what happens to it (for example, that it was delivered or bounced). Resend sends our emails from the EU (Ireland) and keeps its records of them, including your email address and their delivery, in the United States, under its data processing agreement with us. If an email to you bounces permanently or you mark it as spam, we stop emailing that address, and we keep the address on our do-not-email list so it stays that way.

whatYouEnter.title: What you enter
whatYouEnter.body: You control what goes into MTB3A: client names and contact details, projects, income records, optional expenses, notes, and any receipts you attach. It's sent to our servers so it can be stored with your account. On iPhone, you can share a photo or PDF of a receipt into MTB3A. It's uploaded to private cloud storage and attached to the expense. Receipts you upload may be read automatically on MTB3A's own servers, to suggest the amount, date, currency and vendor. The reading is done by software we run ourselves: no outside AI or OCR company ever sees your receipts, and no AI language model reads them. We don't keep the text read from a receipt, only the suggested fields, and you review them before you save the expense.

localMode.title: Trying MTB3A without an account
localMode.body: You can use the web portal without signing in. MTB3A then runs entirely in your browser: what you enter is kept in that browser's storage on your device, and none of it is sent to our servers. Your records leave the device only if you download them as a file from Your data. We can't see, back up or recover them, so if you clear your browser's data or lose the device, they're gone, and they can't be moved into an account later. The portal's pages still load from our servers, and the anonymous count described under "Anonymous usage counts" and the error reports described under "Error reports" work the same way.

issuedDocuments.title: Tax documents and the Israel Tax Authority
issuedDocuments.body: If issuing is turned on for your business profile, you can issue Israeli tax documents with MTB3A: tax invoices, tax invoice-receipts, receipts and credit notes, and payment requests, which are not tax documents. A document holds your business details (name, VAT or company number, address and logo), your client's (name and, where you give them, VAT or company number and address), and its lines, amounts and VAT. When you type a client's company or nonprofit number, we can look it up in Israel's public registries on data.gov.il to fill in the name and address; only the number is sent. To get an allocation number for an invoice that needs one, you connect your profile to the Israel Tax Authority with your own sign-in there. Each time you issue such an invoice, we send the Tax Authority the details its system asks for, among them your and your client's VAT numbers and the document's number, date and amounts, and we keep the number it returns on the document. The keys for that connection are encrypted before we store them. Each document's PDF is signed electronically, so it can be shown not to have changed. Issued documents can't be edited or deleted: a mistake is corrected with a credit note or a new document, as the bookkeeping rules require. How long we keep them is described under "How long we keep information". We may have to hand documents we keep to the Tax Authority, or another authority, when the law gives it the power to ask.

connectedApps.title: Malafat and apps you connect
connectedApps.body: If your firm uses Malafat, a practice management product, it can connect a business profile to MTB3A, and that profile's records are then shared with Malafat, as described under "Who else handles your data". If you sign in with Malafat, Malafat confirms to us who you are, and we link that sign-in to an existing MTB3A account only after you have signed in to it yourself. When you use MTB3A from inside Malafat, Malafat acts for you, with your permission, and only on the profiles connected to your firm. If you connect another app or assistant to your account where MTB3A offers it, that app can read or add the records you allow it to until you disconnect it, and what it does with them is governed by its own privacy policy.

network.title: What reaches the network
network.body: The website's account-request form sends what you type in it to Netlify when you press Send. Each time you open the website's home page, it asks our servers whether sign-up and the free plan are open. That request carries nothing about you, but like any request it reaches our servers with your IP address and browser details, which go into the technical logs described under "No ads, no tracking". The website also sends the error reports described under "Error reports" to Sentry and the anonymous visit counts described under "Anonymous usage counts" to PostHog. The hosted portal connects to MTB3A's servers and, if you turned on anonymous usage, to PostHog. The hosted portal also sends the error reports described under "Error reports" to Sentry, and its sign-up and password-recovery pages connect to Cloudflare Turnstile for the check described under "When you create an account". Its share-link and accountant-invite pages, which anyone with the link can open, connect to MTB3A's servers, to the private storage that holds receipts when someone opens one, and to PostHog for the anonymous counts described under "Anonymous usage counts". The mobile apps connect to MTB3A's servers, to Sentry for error reports, to the private storage that holds your receipts, and, if you turned on anonymous usage, to PostHog, always over encrypted connections.

sharing.title: Who else handles your data
sharing.body: We don't sell your data or share it with advertisers. Our servers and receipt storage run on Google Cloud, which processes the data only to host it for us. Narabnd Studio Ltd, a related company registered in Israel, connects to the Israel Tax Authority and signs issued documents for us, and handles data only on our behalf and under our instructions. When a receipt is read to suggest its fields, our own software does it on those servers, so no other company reads it. Cloudflare carries the connections between you and our hosted portal and servers, and runs the Turnstile check described under "When you create an account". Resend sends our emails, as described under "Emails we send". Stripe handles payments: when you subscribe, it receives your name, your email address, the billing address you give us and a random internal ID for your account, and you type your card details on Stripe's own checkout page, so they never reach our servers. Sentry, hosted in the EU, receives the error reports described under "Error reports" and stores them for us. Our website runs on Netlify, which receives the account-request form and checks each request for spam with Akismet (made by Automattic). PostHog, hosted in the EU, processes the anonymous usage counts described under "Anonymous usage counts" for us. Emails you send to info@mtb3a.com are kept by Microsoft, which hosts our mailbox. Business profiles connected to an organization that uses Malafat share their records with Malafat, as described under "Malafat and apps you connect"; profiles you create yourself never do unless you connect them. The Israel Tax Authority receives the details of the invoices you ask an allocation number for, and data.gov.il the company numbers you look up, as described under "Tax documents and the Israel Tax Authority". If you invite an accountant, they can read the profile you shared with them, as described under "Sharing with your accountant", and anyone you give a share link and its PIN can read the period it covers, as described under "Share links". You choose these people, and files they download are their copy, held under their own responsibilities. Beyond that, we disclose data only when the law, a court order or a competent authority requires it, or when we need it to defend a legal claim. If MTB3A is transferred to another company, your information passes to it only on condition that it keeps the protections in this policy, and we'll tell you first.

accountant.title: Sharing with your accountant
accountant.body: If you own a profile, you can invite your accountant to read it. You type their email address, and we email them an invite, in the language you're using, that works for 14 days and names you and the profile. The invite can be accepted from that address, or by a colleague signed in with an address at the same business's own domain (never a shared email service such as Gmail). Once it's accepted, your accountant can read that one profile: its expenses, income and payments received, receipts, currency conversions and totals, and the clients and projects they belong to. They can download an Excel report and a zip of the receipts for whole months. They can't add, change or delete anything. You see who has access, when they accepted and when they last viewed the profile. You can end their access at any time, and they can stop on their own. Revoking access stops new access right away, but files your accountant (or someone you gave a link) already downloaded are their copy, held under their own responsibilities. We can't recall them. We keep the record of who you invited, when access started and ended, and when it was last used, as part of the profile's history for as long as the profile exists, and delete it with the profile. What happens to this access when you or your accountant close an account is described under "Deleting your account and data".

shareLinks.title: Share links
shareLinks.body: If you own a profile, you can also create a link that lets someone read part of it without an account: the last one, two or three whole months, or everything up to the day you create the link. You choose a PIN of 4 to 8 digits and how long the link works: 1, 7 or 30 days. We show you the link once. We store only a scrambled fingerprint of the link and of the PIN, never the link or the PIN themselves, so we can't show you either again. Until someone enters the right PIN, the page shows nothing about you or the profile, and after 5 wrong PINs the link locks for good. With the PIN, they can read that period's expenses and payments received, with their notes, receipts and totals and the clients, projects and categories they belong to, and download an Excel report and a zip of the receipts for months in it. They can't change anything. A link opens on at most 3 devices, and each device's access lasts up to 8 hours before the PIN is asked again. You can turn a link off at any time, and it stops working when it expires. Files downloaded through a link are that person's copy, and we can't recall them. Of the people who open a link, we keep only what we need to count devices and stop guessing: for each device, a scrambled fingerprint of a random token, when it first and last opened the link, and when its access ends. The page keeps that token in the browser until the link ends, so the device keeps its place among the 3. We use a visitor's IP address briefly, in memory, to slow down repeated attempts, and don't store it. When a link has been over for 30 days, we delete its devices' records; the link's own record (its period, dates and whether it locked) stays in the profile's history for as long as the profile exists.

abroad.title: Information stored outside Israel
abroad.body: MTB3A's servers, database, receipts and backups are in Google Cloud's europe-west1 region in Belgium, in the European Union. Some of the providers listed under "Who else handles your data" keep information in other countries: Resend keeps its records of the emails we send in the United States, Google Cloud's technical logs may be stored outside europe-west1, Cloudflare carries connections through its worldwide network, and Stripe processes payments in the countries its own policy lists. We use these providers under agreements that protect your information as the law requires. We don't keep a copy of your information in Israel today. [TODO(MUT-732, lawyer Q1): whether the transfer regulations or the Tax Authority's rules for invoicing software (for example a copy of issued documents kept in Israel) require more here.]

security.title: Keeping the mobile apps secure
security.body: Your password is stored on our servers only as a secure hash, and never on your phone. Your sign-in session is kept in the iPhone Keychain or in Android's encrypted storage. On your phone, the app's records are protected by your phone's own encryption, and from version 0.1.13 they're left out of iCloud and Google backups. You can turn on App Lock so opening the app needs Face ID, Touch ID, your fingerprint, or your device passcode. That check happens on your device, and MTB3A never receives your biometric data. The mobile apps don't use your camera, contacts, or location, and they only see a photo or file when you choose to share it into the app.

dataSecurity.title: How we protect your information
dataSecurity.body: We protect your information with measures that follow the Data Security Regulations. Connections to MTB3A are encrypted; the database, receipts and backups are encrypted where they are stored; passwords are kept only as secure hashes; the keys for Tax Authority connections are encrypted; and only the small team that runs MTB3A can reach production systems, with changes made through our admin tools logged. You can protect your account further with a passkey and two-step sign-in. If you turn on two-step sign-in, we keep your authenticator app's secret encrypted, and your recovery codes only in a scrambled form. We also keep a security log of sign-ins, two-step checks and Tax Authority connections, with the IP address and browser of each, encrypted, for 12 months, as the Tax Authority's security rules for invoicing software require; it is stored in the same Google Cloud region as your records. No system is completely secure. If a security incident puts your information at risk, we will tell you, and the Privacy Protection Authority, as the law requires. The basic security level under the Protection of Privacy Regulations (Data Security), 5777-2017, applies to our databases.

noTracking.title: No ads, no tracking
noTracking.body: None of MTB3A's apps use advertising or tracking that follows you across sites or apps. Our website, our servers, the hosted portal, and the iPhone and Android apps send error reports when something breaks, as described under "Error reports". The anonymous usage counts we do keep are described under "Anonymous usage counts". Our servers keep technical logs for 30 days (when a request arrived, what it asked for, and whether it succeeded) so we can run the service. Our own log lines never include your IP address. Google Cloud's record of each request includes the address that connected, which is usually Cloudflare's rather than yours. Our servers use your IP address only briefly, in memory, to slow down repeated attempts such as wrong passwords, and pass it to Cloudflare Turnstile for the check described under "When you create an account". We don't use any of this to profile you.

usageAnalytics.title: Anonymous usage counts
usageAnalytics.body: Where we count usage, we use PostHog, hosted in the EU. We never send amounts, names, notes, contact details, your location, or anything you type, and nothing we send is linked to your account. Our website counts page visits and which buttons are pressed, without cookies and without storing anything on your device. With each count it sends the page's address, the page you came from, any campaign tags in the link (such as utm_source), and whether you're on a computer, tablet or phone. To tell visits apart for a single day, PostHog combines your IP address and browser details into a code that changes every day and keeps neither, so a visit can't be linked to you or to visits on other days. Before you sign in, the portal's welcome screen counts which of its three choices you pick (sign in, create an account, or try it on this device) the same way, without cookies and without storing anything on your device, and sends only that choice, the page's address, the portal's version and its analytics library's version, and its language. The portal's pages for share links and accountant invites count the same way, without cookies and without storing anything on your device for the count, and send nothing about you, the link or the profile: a share link's page counts when a link is opened and which period it covers, and when a file is downloaded (the report or the receipts, and how many months); an invite's page counts when an invite is accepted (signed in or with a new account). Each count carries the same page address, versions and language as the welcome screen's. The hosted portal asks you once whether you want to share anonymous usage, and it's off unless you turn it on. If you do, it sends a short note when you turn it on (saying whether you did so from the prompt or the account menu), each time you open the portal, each time you save an income, an expense or a payment received, and when it shows the free trial's reminder to add a card and whether you chose to add one or not. A note says only which of these it was, its currency, for an income whether it was already paid, and for the trial reminder whether it showed when you first signed in or on your Home page, along with the portal's version and its analytics library's version, its language, your browser's type, your device's operating system and its version, and whether it's a computer, tablet, or phone. Notes are sent under a random ID kept only in your browser, not linked to your account, and replaced when you sign out. If you turn it off from the account menu, we send one last note saying you turned it off, then stop and delete the random ID. The iPhone and Android apps ask you once whether you want to share anonymous usage, and it's off unless you turn it on. If you do, they send a short note each time you turn it on (saying whether you did so from the prompt or Settings), once more the first time you turn it on after signing in, and each time you add a client or save an income or an expense. A note says only which of these it was, its currency, and for an income whether it was already paid, along with the app's version and its analytics library's version, its language, your phone's operating system and its version, and whether it's a phone or a tablet. Notes are sent under a random ID kept only on your phone, not linked to your account, and replaced when you sign out. If you turn it off in Settings, we send one last note saying you turned it off, then stop and delete the random ID. These counts are used only to understand which parts of MTB3A people use. They're never used for advertising, and no one but PostHog, which processes them for us, receives them.

errorReports.title: Error reports
errorReports.body: When something breaks, we want to know before you have to tell us. An error report says where in our code the problem happened, which version you were using, your language, and your device's operating system, browser, and model. Before a report is sent, we remove amounts, names, notes, contact details, request contents, your IP address, and anything you type. When the iPhone or Android app itself crashes, Sentry's own scrubbing removes them instead, because the app can't edit that report first. If a report includes an account at all, it is a random internal ID. Reports are stored by Sentry in the EU. Our servers send a report when a request fails on our side, and the hosted portal sends one when a page crashes in your browser. Our website sends a report when one of its pages crashes or hits an error. The website's reports include no account at all. The iPhone and Android apps send a report when the app crashes or hits an error it can't recover from, and so do the iPhone app's share extension, widgets and Siri shortcuts. They never attach screenshots or what's on your screen.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.body: We use only what MTB3A needs to work, and no advertising or cross-site tracking cookies. When you sign in to the web portal, it sets one session cookie that keeps you signed in; signing in with Malafat sets a short-lived cookie for that sign-in only. The website and the portal remember your language in your browser's storage. If you turn on anonymous usage in the portal, its random ID is kept in your browser, as described under "Anonymous usage counts". A share link's page keeps a random token so your device keeps its place, as described under "Share links", and the portal without an account keeps your records in your browser, as described under "Trying MTB3A without an account". Cloudflare Turnstile, which checks the sign-up and password-recovery forms, may use its own storage to tell people from bots. You can clear all of this in your browser's settings; you'll then be signed out, and records kept without an account will be lost.

retention.title: How long we keep information
retention.body: We keep information only as long as we need it for the purposes above or the law requires. Your account and records: while your account is open, and for 30 days after you ask to close it; then they're deleted, as described under "Deleting your account and data". Tax documents you issued: the bookkeeping rules require them to be kept for 7 years, so we keep each document, and the business details printed on it, for 7 years from the document's own date, even after you close your account, and then delete it. A profile's business details, logo and document numbering go when its last document goes. Until then, a former owner can ask us for the full archive (the signed documents and the uniform file), and we hand it over once we've checked who is asking. If you ask us to erase your documents sooner, we'll do so only after we have given you the full archive to download and told you that you must keep it for 7 years yourself. The security log: 12 months from each event. The count of documents you issue and receipts you scan each month, which applies your plan's limits: each event for 13 months, the monthly totals for 25 months. Daily counts of requests to each part of our servers: 90 days. Our servers' technical logs and our email log: 30 days. Backups: 14 days. Error reports: until Sentry's retention ends. Requests sent through our website's form or by email: up to 12 months. Payment invoices kept by Stripe: as long as tax law requires.

mobileDeletion.title: Deleting your account and data
mobileDeletion.body: You can delete individual entries at any time. To delete your whole account, choose Close my account: in the web portal under You › Account, or in the iPhone and Android apps on the Account tab. For 30 days you can sign in and keep your account; after that, we delete it. A business profile you share with someone who also owns it passes to them. If other people work in it and none of them is an owner, make one of them an owner, or remove them, before you close your account. Once you ask to close your account, your accountants and your share links can't open the profiles you own; if you keep your account, they work again. When your account is deleted, the accountants' access and the share links of the profiles we delete go with them, and a profile that passes to a co-owner keeps its accountants and links. If you're an accountant, your access to the profiles shared with you is deleted with your account. We delete your account, the profiles you own with every record and receipt in them, your sign-ins, passkeys, two-step sign-in settings and recovery codes, the record that you accepted our terms, and your customer record at Stripe. On profiles that stay because you didn't own them, the records you added stay, without your name. We keep: in those profiles' history, a note that a removed account (a random internal ID, never your name or email) was deleted; at Stripe, the invoices for what you paid, which tax law requires us to keep; the tax documents you issued with MTB3A and the business details printed on them, each for 7 years from its own date, as described under "How long we keep information" (until then, write to us and we'll send you the full archive once we've checked it's you; once you have it, you can ask us to delete them sooner, as described there); for 12 months from each event, the security log of your sign-ins, two-step checks and Tax Authority connections; your address on our do-not-email list, if you asked us to stop emailing it; for up to 30 days, our email log and our servers' logs, which hold the internal ID or a scrambled form of your address; error reports with the internal ID, until Sentry's retention ends; Resend's records of the emails we sent you; and, if you sent our website's request form or wrote to us, your message, until we delete it within 12 months. Deleted receipt files can be recovered for 14 days, and copies in our backups clear 14 days after deletion. Signing out of the mobile app ends your session. On iPhone, the app's sign-in record can stay in the Keychain until you reinstall the app. Copies of the app's data in iCloud or Google backups made before version 0.1.13 can remain until those backups are replaced.

yourRights.title: Your rights
yourRights.body: Under the Protection of Privacy Law, you may ask to see the information we hold about you, and to have it corrected or deleted if it is wrong, incomplete, unclear or out of date. You can also get a copy of your records as a file (most of it you can download yourself from Your data), close your account, withdraw your consent to usage counts at any time, and stop promotional emails with the Unsubscribe link in them (or ask us to stop emailing you anything but what your account needs). Where the GDPR applies, you may also ask us to restrict or stop using your information and to receive it in a portable form. Write to info@mtb3a.com from your account's email address; we may ask you to confirm it's you. We answer within 30 days, and if we refuse a request we tell you why. Some information we can't delete while the law requires us to keep it, such as issued tax documents, and an issued document is corrected with a new one, never edited. If your details are in records someone else keeps in MTB3A (for example, you are a client of a business that uses it), ask that business first; we'll help it answer. You may also complain to Israel's Privacy Protection Authority or, in the EU or the UK, to your data protection authority.

children.title: Children's privacy
children.body: MTB3A is a tool for running a business and is meant for people aged 18 or over. We don't knowingly collect information from children. If you believe a child has given us information, write to us and we'll delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy as MTB3A or the law changes. We'll update this page and the "Last updated" date above. If a change materially affects how we use your information, we'll tell you by email or in the portal and the apps before it takes effect, and where a change needs your consent, we'll ask for it.

hostedRequest.title: When you ask for an account
hostedRequest.body: If you send the request form on our website, Netlify, which hosts the website, receives what you type: your name, your email and anything else you choose to add, plus the language the page was in and a random request number. Netlify also records technical details such as your IP address and browser, and checks the request for spam with Akismet. Netlify then emails it to us. We use it only to reply with an offer and, if you go ahead, to set up your account. We delete requests within 12 months; write to info@mtb3a.com and we'll delete yours sooner.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions about this policy, requests about your information and complaints can be sent to info@mtb3a.com. We reply within 2 working days. By post: Barmajiyat Ltd, 65 London Wall, London, United Kingdom.

pilotSessions.title: Watched pilot sessions
pilotSessions.body: If you join our free pilot, we ask you once whether we may watch you use MTB3A, and record your screen, in sessions we arrange with you. We keep your answer and its date with your account. If you say no, the pilot works the same and we do not watch or record you. A recording is used only to improve MTB3A, stays with us and is never shared. [TODO: how long recordings are kept, and where.] Our usage counts never record your screen.
